clue.text: Dominant influence, say, breaching border on conclusion of foray

indicators.note: something breaching a barrier breaks into it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hem is the folded border of a piece of cloth

taken as written

parts.note: the final letter of foray

explanation.surface: A raid across a frontier is presented as an exercise in dominance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is a standard signal for an example, written as the abbreviation for exempli gratia.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegemony is the leadership or control exercised by one state or group over others.

clue.text: Immoderate Frenchman dodging less important girlfriend, keeping home

someone dodging is absent, so the Frenchman's letter drops out

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for monsieur
minor means of lesser importance
a date is a person one is going out with
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A Frenchman excessively avoids his lesser girlfriend by staying indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frenchman' is the abbreviation for monsieur, not a word like Pierre; 'home' is the common crossword sense of being in.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means unreasonably large or excessive, going beyond proper limits.

clue.text: Relish what is usually a morning activity

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sauce or condiment such as salad ...

definitions.text: what is usually a morning activity
definitions.meaning: second meaning: putting on clothes after getting up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a verb meaning enjoy; here it is a noun for a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing is a sauce poured over food, and dressing is also the act of putting clothes on.

clue.text: Walk slowly and walk clumsily, with top half twisted

indicators.note: in a down entry the top half turned round means those first letters are read backwards

parts.note: to waddle is to walk with short swaying steps, like a duck

explanation.surface: Someone ambles along and lurches about with their upper body twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first three letters of WADDLE are turned round; the rest stays, giving DAWDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle is to move idly and take more time than needed.

clue.text: British politician leaving British dominion for another country

indicators.note: the politician leaving means those letters depart from the dominion's word

parts.note: the British Empire was Britain's dominion overseas
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A British politician quits the Empire to go and live abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: EMPIRE without MP leaves EIRE, fittingly a country that left British rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, a nation distinct from Britain.

clue.text: Useless grant producing rant if so?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: worthless, of no help
second meaning, cryptic: G is short for good, and the word grant without it is rant

explanation.surface: A worthless grant leads only to angry ranting.
explanation.walkthrough: G is a standard abbreviation for good, so 'no good' means taking G away, which turns grant into rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no good is worthless and of no help to anyone.

clue.text: Former queen, English, with spare soldiers

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
spare and lean both mean thin, with no excess
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A queen of old, English, with soldiers in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleanor of Aquitaine and Eleanor of Castile were both English queens.
explanation.definitionFit: Several medieval queens consort of England bore this name, so it fits a royal of the past.

clue.text: Augment encore, possibly, crying for more?

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: all thirteen letters are used

explanation.surface: An audience calling for more to extend an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: shouting 'more!' urges performers on.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts demanding more from performers are a form of urging and support.

clue.text: American started to eat, displaying poor taste

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
to bite off a piece is to begin eating it, here in the past tense

explanation.surface: An American tucks in with bad table manners.
explanation.walkthrough: A bit off is a British phrase for slightly improper or unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour described as slightly improper or unacceptable shows lapses in good manners.

clue.text: Given new perspective, therefore nods after reconsideration

indicators.note: reconsidering something means thinking it over again, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: all thirteen letters are used

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders and so nods agreement, with a fresh view.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreshortening shows an object as shorter than it is because of the viewing angle, an effect of perspective.

clue.text: Less expensive, reduced by a penny? Some measure of enthusiasm here

indicators.note: reduced by means made smaller by taking away what follows

parts.note: cheaper means costing less
taken as written
p is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A bargain knocked down by a penny prompts a little enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A and P from CHEAPER leaves CHEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheer is a shout of approval, one way of showing excitement.

clue.text: Battle stations at first beside border area after retreat

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of stations
an edge is a border

indicators.note: a retreat is a movement backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: room means space or area

explanation.surface: Troops take up positions near a frontier region after pulling back.
explanation.walkthrough: Sedgemoor in Somerset was the site of the 1685 battle that ended Monmouth's rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Sedgemoor was the last pitched battle fought on English soil.

clue.text: Crime in union? Union initially cross over progress involving detectives mostly

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so one piece holds the other
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes
initially means at the start, so the first letter is taken

an X is a cross
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
to ride is to proceed or travel along
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A crime within a trade union, involving an angry union member and detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' in the definition is marriage, not a trade union; uxoricide is the killing of one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Murdering a wife is a crime committed within a marriage, which is a union of two people.

clue.text: Not entirely right to involve US lawyer for traitor

indicators.note: to involve means to take in, so one piece surrounds the other
not entirely means one letter short of the whole word

parts.note: just means right or fair
a DA is a District Attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A US lawyer is drawn into something not quite right, betraying a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' here is fair or deserved, not the direction; a District Attorney is the American public prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his name became a byword for a betrayer.

clue.text: Opinions intended to dismiss article probing Biblical book

indicators.note: something probing pushes inside, so it sits within the other word

parts.note: Judges is a book of the Old Testament

indicators.note: dismissing something sends it away, so the article is removed

parts.note: meant means intended
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Planned views drop an article examining scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Biblical book is the Old Testament one recounting Israel's leaders before the kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Judgements are views or conclusions formed after consideration.

clue.text: Some area normally left empty

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: a word left empty has its insides removed, so only its outside letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of normally

explanation.surface: A region that is usually left vacant.
explanation.definitionFit: Some and any are both determiners meaning an unspecified amount, as in 'have you any bread?'

clue.text: Get on with Communist, keeping Nationalist annoyed

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the next letter goes inside

parts.note: to get on is to grow older, to age
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist
a Red is a common term for a Communist

explanation.surface: A Communist and a Nationalist failing to get along, with tempers rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' suggests getting along with someone; here it means growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Angered and annoyed both describe someone made cross or irritated.

clue.text: Broadcaster had Maori in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: all eight letters are used

explanation.surface: A presenter featured a Maori guest on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio ham is an amateur radio operator who transmits messages over the airwaves.

clue.text: Year that never existed for business

explanation.surface: A trading business named after a year that never happened.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the zero as the letter O: AD plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, as in 'much ado about nothing', a sense of commotion or business.

clue.text: After beer a politician is unpredictable

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the drink's word leads and the rest follows

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician after a drink becomes erratic.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory means depending on chance, from the Latin for a dice player.

clue.text: Follow university in various points

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

parts.note: east, north, south and east are compass points
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Students track a university across several locations.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points supply single letters: E, N, S, W.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to happen afterwards as a result.

clue.text: Work steadily in pursuit of drink in amount provided

indicators.note: something in pursuit of another comes behind it, so it is placed second

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
to ply a trade is to work at it steadily

explanation.definitionFit: A supply is a stock or quantity of something made available.

clue.text: Deposit: dodgy gold, by chaps investing in film

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: E.T. is the 1982 Spielberg film
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Crooked gold being banked by men putting money into a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' looks like a verb; here it is a noun, a lodgement being something lodged or deposited.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodgement is a sum paid into a bank account, or matter that has collected somewhere.

clue.text: Woolly old sheep's heading into track

indicators.note: into means going inside the next word

parts.note: a lane is a narrow track or road
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: a heading is at the top, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of sheep

explanation.surface: An old woolly sheep makes its way along a path.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanose is a rare word meaning covered in fine hair, like wool, from Latin lana.

clue.text: Exotic language playing on repeat has son engrossed

indicators.note: something engrossed is absorbed into another, so the son's letter goes inside
playing with letters means moving them round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.walkthrough: The S joins the letters of 'on repeat' before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented language, unusual in having no native country.

clue.text: Singer in Germany may include this tetralogy

explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Wagner's Ring cycle, a work a singer in Germany may well include.
explanation.definitionFit: Der Ring des Nibelungen is Wagner's cycle of four operas, so it forms a set of four works.

clue.text: Some dupe at Enfield is taken in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests being fooled, matching dupe; here it means swallowed.

clue.text: Part of Bible engaged in stories: here's subject of parable

parts.note: tales are stories

explanation.surface: A section of scripture told as stories, with a parable's subject.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the Parable of the Talents is itself in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Parable of the Talents, servants are entrusted with sums of money called talents.

clue.text: Prepared a bit of tea? No longer fresh

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece, here its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of tea
